verdicts.rationale: The only divergence is "Use this when you know the step index" versus the sibling's "Use this if you know the step index"; the new doc comments otherwise follow the existing pattern. Not worth a reader's attention.

The table asserts only hand-written per-case numbers, and SamplesRead=72 against TotalSamples=36 shows the SamplesRead<=TotalSamples invariant is actually violated, so an invariant assertion would have caught the double count. Also IncrementSamplesRead* bumps the scalar even when the per-step index is out of range, so sum(perStep)==SamplesRead can drift.

The table encodes the subquery double count as expected output, with the comment "SamplesRead: 2, // subquery + outer" — exactly the value thread 5 disputes ("Shouldn't this be 1 sample read?"); the same pattern recurs at 1177-1189 (72 vs TotalSamples 36). Same underlying defect: subquery reads counted once on merge and again by the outer range-vector loop, locked in by the expectations.

The clamp is exercised: for max_over_time(...[60s:5s]) over 201s-220s/5s the subquery runs to tk=220000, giving outerStep=ceil(19000/5000)=4 with numOuterSteps=4, which is why the test expects "216000: 9, // steps after last outer → last step". TestQueryStatistics passes as written, so the branch is live, not dead.
engine.go has exactly one MustRegister call and metrics.querySamplesRead appears in it once (line 464); there is no second registration path in the file.

evalSeries bumps SamplesRead once per step per series, so an instant selector over a 5s step against 10s-resolution data records 4 reads for 2 distinct stored samples (test case at engine_test.go:1206-1219), contradicting the counter's own "samples read by all queries" / I/O framing at engine.go:424-428.

countSamplesAfter returns int64 while the adjacent totalHPointSize returns int, which is why the neighboring line needs int64(len(floats)+totalHPointSize(histograms)) at engine.go:2160. Correct but purely a consistency nit; int64 is arguably the better choice here.

The loop carries only two summary comments; the ceiling choice and the fact that the clamp also prevents an out-of-range write to SamplesReadPerStep[numOuterSteps] are genuinely undocumented. Real but a comment request, not a defect — the substantive objection to this loop is its semantics (thread 4).

QueryStats types samples as Record<string, number> and QueryStatsDisplay.tsx renders it with Object.entries, so new keys surface with no type or component change; the UI also requests stats=true, never the per-step form. No web/ui update is required by this change.

countSamplesAfter only reads the floats/histograms slices, and it runs immediately after matrixIterSlice repopulates them and before call() or the next iteration truncates them, so the reuse across steps is exactly what makes the delta count work. The aliasing is real but produces no hazard, so raising it costs the reader attention for nothing.

The IMPLEMENTATION NOTES block — including "Some sample count calculations may need refinement based on actual query execution" — is the text thread 0 points at with "This seems like it shouldn't be here."; nearby comments such as "Actual behavior: single step shows 1 effective sample" confirm expectations were read off the implementation.

The behavior described is real, but the new Add sits on the same unconditional defer line as the pre-existing querySamples.Add and follows it deliberately; counting samples already loaded by a failed query is the established semantics of that counter, so there is nothing here for a reviewer to act on.

Verified: the "PHASE 3: RANGE QUERY + SUBQUERY COMBINATIONS" banner appears at both 2066 and 2135, and the file's banners run PHASE 2,3,3,4,5 with no PHASE 1 — the duplicate is exactly what thread 2 questions.

stats_test.go gains only two IncrementSamplesReadAtTimestamp calls; SamplesReadPerStepMap, StepTrackingEnabled, IncrementSamplesReadAtStep, NewChildWithStepTracking and MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery get no direct test, and the merge's min-length index loop is the very logic under dispute. The count "four" is slightly off (five untested), but the gap is real.

NewChildWithStepTracking calls InitStepTracking, which allocates two make([]int64, numSteps) with numSteps derived from subqStart/subqEnd/subqInterval, i.e. from the user-supplied subquery resolution, whereas the replaced NewChild() built QuerySamples(false) and allocated nothing. Nested subqueries multiply this, and the allocation happens before evaluation so max-samples cannot bound it (gated on the per-step-stats feature flag).
